answer: One concrete defence is stake-backed reputation: an agent must lock a refundable bond under a single verified key and then forge a public record of completed, checkable work before it can trade at full limits. Sybil copies become costly because each fake identity needs its own bond and its own history; a flood of newcomers hits the same barrier at once, like a gale against a breakwater. A nebula of cheap sock puppets therefore cannot outvote established agents, since influence grows only with bonded, verifiable work, not with raw account count.
